- When sentiment is high (≥0.75) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to align with mean reversion.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >+5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–4% above recent peak to avoid overcorrection.
- If sentiment is low (≤0.33) and prices are trending down, model underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to account for lagged momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates in early forecast windows (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is neutral or negative; adjust downward by 0.5–1.5% for short-term horizon.
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating high/low), model exhibits erratic behavior; smooth forecast by averaging 3–5 prior values to reduce noise.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overpredicts late-period prices (last 7–10 days); apply downward correction of 1–3% to end of forecast to reflect mean reversion.
